## Maintainer ruling recorded — **A: self-service through the generic data path, in the `sys_api_key` shape, with the ADR-0092 D5 amendment** (2026-09-03)

**Provenance.** Ruled by the maintainer (pm@objectstack.ai) in the director seat's live session (`session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`), decision batch #22, 2026-09-03 after 15:35Z. Verbatim reply: 「同意」. The batch was presented with this card's recommendation as **A** (fallback C; B rejected as a second write path for the same column; D refused on #13881's measurement), so 「同意」 adopts A. Ledger: objectstack#12708, batch #22 ledger comment.

**What was ruled.** A rank-and-file member may edit their own `sys_user` row on the generic data path, bounded on two axes that already exist:
- **who / which rows** — `member_default` gains an explicit `sys_user` entry (`allowRead` / `allowEdit` true, create / delete false) in `plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts`, and the `sys_user_self` RLS policy widens from `select` to cover the update, so the caller reaches their own row and no other;
- **which columns** — the identity write guard keeps bounding a user-context update to the ADR-0092 D2 whitelist `{name, image, locale}`; nothing else on the row opens.
- **ADR-0092 D5 is amended** to say so: self-service edits of the whitelisted columns route through the generic data path, with the D6 `afterUpdate` hook as the session-cache refresh. `name` / `image` therefore also become editable on that path; the mechanism PR #14958 already touches carries it, and the amendment records it as ruled rather than incidental.
- ⛔ Not B (a dedicated endpoint under system context — the "second stamping route" #14787's ruling rejected, one level up). ⛔ Not C (a user-facing setting only an administrator can set). ⛔ Not D.

**Execution.** `domain:services` lane. The ADR amendment lives under `docs/adr/**` (governed): draft, the maintainer merges by hand; the seat may split it from the code PR, in which case the code PR is not armed before the ADR PR merges. Pins: own-row `locale` update succeeds; another member's row is refused; `name` / `image` on the generic path succeed and the session refresh is observed; a non-whitelisted column is still refused by the guard. Changeset required. **Clause-②: yes** (permission-set defaults move) — `needs:contract-review` carrier on the PR. objectui#7501 unblocks when this lands.

**State.** `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke; `priority:p2`, `domain:services`, `i18n` kept; unassigned.

**Ruling of record — comments read: 1, to the last page, and it IS the ruling: `issuecomment-5528362189`** (2026-09-03 15:53:33Z). Reading it mattered: the card **body** ends by recommending A and saying it "必须由维护者裁", which on its own reads as an undispatched decision card wearing a queue label. It is not — the maintainer ruled **A** in decision batch #22 (verbatim 「同意」), and the ruling comment records `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke. Acting on the body alone would have flipped a ruled card back into the decision box.

Dispatching to implement **A as ruled**, not to re-open it.

## PM ACCEPT — PRs #15108 (code) + #15109 (ADR), head `d845d564ec`. Verified against the tree, not the report.

`domain:services` execution seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`. Ruling A implemented as ruled; ⛔ nothing about its substance reopened.

### Verified independently at the PR head

| claim | reading |
|---|---|
| `member_default` gains the ruled `sys_user` entry | `default-permission-sets.ts:529` — `{ allowRead: true, allowCreate: false, allowEdit: true, allowDelete: false }`. Exactly the ruled shape. |
| `sys_user_self` widened | `:636-638` — `operation: 'all'` |
| ⭐ `sys_user_org_members` NOT widened | `:650-652` — `operation: 'select'`, unchanged |
| the ADR link placeholder | `ADR_PR_URL` now appears **0** times in #15108's body; #15109 is linked explicitly |

### ⭐ The dev found a security distinction this dispatch did not name

The dispatch ordered the `sys_user_self` widening. It said nothing about the sibling policy. The dev worked out that **applicable policies OR-combine**, so widening the org-peer visibility policy alongside it would have composed an update filter of

```
id == me  OR  id IN <every user in my organization>
```

— handing every rank-and-file member write access to their colleagues' rows, while looking like the same one-line change. It left `sys_user_org_members` at `select`, pinned the distinction in three places, and wrote the hazard into the source at `:629-631` so the next reader (or the next agent) does not "tidy up" the asymmetry.

That is the same shape as the asymmetric-pair hazard this lane hit on #14949/#15030 two rounds ago, caught this time before it shipped rather than after.

### The phantom-pin hazard the dispatch DID name is closed, and measured

The dispatch warned that pin 4 could pass because the object gate refuses before the identity guard is ever reached. The dev made layer attribution **mechanical** rather than asserted: middleware throws with `ql.findOne` never called ⇒ object-gate; throws with `findOne` called ⇒ row-scope; passes and the guard hook throws ⇒ identity-guard. It drives the real SecurityPlugin middleware over the real shipped permission sets and the real `SysUser` schema, answering `findOne` by evaluating the filter the middleware actually composed against a two-row fixture — so the row scope is a measurement, not a stub. All four verdicts are produced by the suite, which is its own non-vacuity control.

Predictions were written to a file **before** either ablation leg ran. Both matched exactly:

- **Leg A** (revert the whole permission-set file): predicted 9 red / 3 green + 6 red; measured the same. The two discriminating failures are the point — *"expected object-gate to be row-scope"* and *"expected object-gate to be identity-guard"*. ⇒ before this change, **both pins would have passed at the wrong layer**. The hazard was real.
- **Leg B** (revert only the RLS widening, keeping the object entry): predicted 9 red / 3 green + 3 red; measured the same, with pin 4 now reading *"expected row-scope to be identity-guard"* — independent evidence that the which-rows half is load-bearing for the guard being reached at all.

Mutation and restore were both proved on disk by blob hash rather than by an editor's exit code.

Four gates answered **exit 3 = NOT MEASURED**, each named with why the diff cannot move it. That is the correct reading; ⛔ exit 3 is not a pass.

### Landing order — unchanged

⛔ **#15108 is not armed until #15109 merges.** `docs/adr/**` is governed; the maintainer merges it by hand. `needs:contract-review` stays on #15108 (Clause-② yes — permission-set defaults move) and ⛔ is not cleared here.

`#14951` (ADR-0092 D1's tier table still listing two members against an enforced three) was already on the backlog; the dev confirmed by search rather than assuming, left it alone, and the amendment names it as not-amended-here so a D5 reader is not misled.

## Ordering constraint discharged

PR #15108 carried an explicit ⛔ *"Do not arm this PR for merge before the ADR PR lands."* That constraint is now satisfied, not waived:

- **PR #15109 (the ADR-0092 D5 amendment) MERGED at `2026-09-04T03:21:43Z`**, merged by `hotlong`. Read off `merged_at` — not `auto_merge` (GitHub clears it on enqueue) and not `merge_commit_sha` (that is the test-merge commit and is populated while `merged` is still false).
- Only then was #15108 taken out of draft and armed.

Order of operations was **undraft first, then arm** — auto-merge does not survive a draft→ready conversion, so arming a draft PR silently buys nothing.

## Carrier state, verified rather than assumed

`needs:contract-review` is **absent from both** PR #15108 and this card, which is the correct end state: the contract review PASSED at tier via the director seat at `01:32:23Z` (`14959#issuecomment-5534395446`, verdict "PASS, landing held", with landing explicitly delegated to this seat once the ADR PR was in).

⚠️ Stated precisely because the evidence does not distinguish it: a gate-carrier label that has been stripped is indistinguishable from one that was never applied — a missing gate label reads as *green light*, not as red. What makes the clearance sound here is the PASS comment above, not the absent label.

## Checks at the armed head `d845d564ec`

44 check runs, **zero `failure` conclusions**; combined status `success`. Two runs were re-triggered at `03:22:0xZ` when the base moved under the #15109 merge — `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Check Changeset` — and were still `in_progress` at arm time. That is not a reason to hold the arm: auto-merge waits on required checks by construction. If either comes back red the PR simply will not merge, and this seat handles it.

## What remains

On MERGED: strip `pm:dispatched` from this card and post the landing record. This card stays open until then.

Downstream: objectui#7501 (the account-settings "my language" form item) is the consumer this route unblocks — that is a **separate repo and lane**, so it is named here rather than acted on, and the follow-up belongs to whichever seat accepts this PR's product into `objectui`.

Still deliberately untouched: ADR-0092 D1's tier table lists two Tier-1 members while the enforced whitelist constant holds three. That is #14951 and is not a rider on this work.

## What the maintainer's 「同意」 now buys, concretely

A rank-and-file member can set their own `sys_user.locale` on the generic data path — bounded on **which rows** by the `sys_user_self` RLS carve-out and on **which columns** by ADR-0092 D2's identity write guard. `#14788`'s ruling that the stored locale outranks `Accept-Language` *because it is a user-stated preference* is now true rather than aspirational: the user can state it.

The org-peer scope `sys_user_org_members` deliberately stayed `select`-only. That was the load-bearing restraint in the whole change — RLS policies OR-combine, so widening it would have composed "my id OR every user id in my org" and handed every member their colleagues' profile rows.

- **objectui#7501** (account-settings "my language" form item) now has a route to post to. Different repo, different lane — the follow-up belongs to whichever seat accepts this into `objectui`, not to this one.
- **#14951** stays open: ADR-0092 D1's tier *table* still lists two Tier-1 members while the enforced whitelist constant holds three. Deliberately not ridden on either PR.
